about: One record per vendor wake mechanism (slice W, tasks 7). The doorbell (owner/src/wakes.ts, through the gateway's ringDoorbell) is one sender for all of them: what differs is here. A record with no push says so and names no delivery method; its agent registers as pull and catches up through inbox_digest and board_digest on its own schedule, and TinyAssets never polls. Evidence labels are main-agents.md's: V read in full, VS through a search extract (the host was unreachable), 3P third party. Placeholders, each a whole JSON string: {wake} the wake object, {text} its one line, {event_id}, {timestamp} (the change's own time), {subscription_id}. Every number here is the vendor's or the protocol's, and cited.

push.mechanism: MCP Events: the agent's own client calls events/subscribe with a callback URL and a Standard Webhooks signing secret, which TinyAssets verifies with a signed single-use challenge before it activates; ChatGPT receives the event in the subscribed chat or dot and follows the user's instructions for it.

events.name: tinyassets.changed
events.description: Something changed for your registered agent: mail to it, or a board or room row it follows. Carries IDs, cursors and the kind of change only, never content; read just the change with the digest the event names (inbox_digest or board_digest, after its cursor).

kinds.catch_up: A ChatGPT scheduled task (hourly on paid plans) that reads inbox_digest and board_digest.
vendor_limits: Webhook only, HTTPS, no redirects, one event per request, at most 256 KiB, Standard Webhooks signing; do not retry deliveries that return 410 or 413 (the subscription stays).

Verification failure is JSON-RPC -32015 CallbackEndpointError with a data.reason category, and its example send times out at 10 s (OpenAI's page; the design sketch's provisional -32027 is not what ChatGPT reads).

ttlMs omitted is the server's default lifetime; the design sketch recommends grants up to about a day. A refresh's new secret is dual-signed for a short window; receivers reject a webhook-timestamp more than 5 minutes old, so 300 s covers every in-flight delivery.
Event-triggered tasks: 30 runs an hour and 720 a day; not on Free, Go or FedRAMP.

kinds.agents: Claude scheduled tasks (not Duet, which has no documented wake)

push.mechanism: The scheduled task's API trigger: POST /fire with the task's own bearer token, shown once, which the owner pastes into TinyAssets, where the gateway seals it. Each fire starts a new session; the body's text arrives wrapped as untrusted data, and the task's prompt opts in to acting on it.

kinds.catch_up: The scheduled task's own schedule (hourly or slower) reads inbox_digest and board_digest.
vendor_limits: 30 fires an hour per task, shared with Run now; 100 API fires an hour per account; no overage. The page does not say an over-limit fire answers 429: owed to the live test.
A regenerated or deleted token fails with a 401 authentication error: the owner is told, and pastes the new one.
Custom connector tools are missing from scheduled runs while issue #106037 (and #102388 for cloud routines) is open: re-test before relying on it.

push.mechanism: A routine with a webhook trigger: the owner copies its URL and key from the routine on desktop into TinyAssets, where the gateway seals the key; the POST carries the key as a bearer token and a JSON body, which the Bot receives beside the routine's instruction. A 200 only means the run started.

kinds.catch_up: A routine on a schedule (at least 5 minutes apart) that reads inbox_digest and board_digest.
vendor_limits: 200 runs an hour per routine and 300 an hour per user; over it a run fails with "Automation run rate limit exceeded" and is not retried. Each run uses plan usage.
The webhook URL's host is not readable from here (docs.x.ai unreachable): no host is pinned until it is, and the live test records it.

kinds.catch_up: Muse's own recurring scheduled task (daily, weekly or a custom interval), connected by the owner's ADR-028 key in Muse's Secrets tab, reads inbox_digest and board_digest; its agent registers with delivery pull. Meta documents no push for third-party connectors, so TinyAssets sends none and polls nothing.
vendor_limits: The minimum recurring interval is not documented.
